series.label: Countries with a national data privacy law (Greenleaf count)
series.geography: World (independent countries and separate legal jurisdictions)
series.notes: Graham Greenleaf's biennial global count, published in Privacy Laws & Business International Report since 2011. A 'data privacy law' in his definition covers most of the private sector (and usually the public sector) and meets minimum formal standards drawn from the OECD Guidelines and Council of Europe Convention 108; separate legal jurisdictions (e.g. Faroe Islands) count as 'countries'. Pre-2011 points are running sums of his 2011 decade counts; his 2025 year-by-year list (SSRN 5189972, 3 pages) could not be retrieved, so points between editions are not interpolated. Counts are as at the date of each edition, not year-end. Average growth 1973-2025: 3.3 new countries a year; since 2020: 5.4 a year.

sources.title: Graham Greenleaf, '172 Countries with Data Privacy Laws - Year by Year 1973-2025' (SSRN 5189972; (2025) 194 PLBIR)
sources.quote: For the past 52 years, since 1973 when Sweden enacted the first national data privacy law, countries around the world have enacted new data privacy laws at an average rate of 3.3 new countries per year, giving a total of 172 countries with such laws by March 2025. Since 2020 the average number of new countries per year has risen to 5.4.

series.label: Share of countries with data protection and privacy legislation (UNCTAD Global Cyberlaw Tracker)
series.unit: % of countries tracked (194 UNCTAD member states; 195 entries in the 2026 data file)
series.notes: UNCTAD's tracker counts any data protection and privacy legislation reported by member states and is broader than Greenleaf's count (which requires minimum international standards and private-sector coverage), so the two series do not match exactly. UNCTAD revised its own figure downward between December 2020 (132/194) and May 2021 (128/194).

sources.title: Data Protection and Privacy Legislation Worldwide (Global Cyberlaw Tracker page), capture of 1 April 2022
sources.quote: 137 out of 194 countries had put in place legislation to secure the protection of data and privacy.
sources.note: The sentence was unchanged in captures through 5 January 2025 (https://web.archive.org/web/20250105191814/https://unctad.org/page/data-protection-and-privacy-legislation-worldwide).

sources.title: Data and privacy unprotected in one third of countries, despite progress (news item)
sources.quote: Concerning data and privacy, 66% of countries have legislation. The share is 96% in Europe, 69% in the Americas, 57% in Asia and the Pacific and 50% in Africa.
sources.note: Survey released 28 April 2020 at UNCTAD eWeek; read via Internet Archive capture (unctad.org returns 403 to scripts).
